Piyush Midtwal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 March,
2025

Author: Sanjeev S Kalgaonkar
Bench: Sanjeev S Kalgaonkar

Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:6829
 1 Mcr
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Indore

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Sanjeev S Kalgaonkar

On The 12th Of March, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 55504 of 2024
 Piyush Midtwal
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Aditya Kumar Bhargava advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Apoorv Joshi public prosecutor for State.
 Shri Nilesh Manore advocate for objector.
 Order

This first application has been filed by applicant under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No. 252/2024 registered at Police Station,
Malharganj District Indore (Urban) (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 376, 376(2)(n),
376(3) of IPC and Sections 5L,6, 3, 4(2), 16 and 17 of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in judicial custody since 29.6.2024.
As per the case of prosecution, mother of victim reported to PS Malharganj that her minor daughter aged around 15 years informed her that she got friendly with Piyush on Instagram.
They were studying in same school.
Piyush once took her to COD Cafe at Malhgarganj and took her photo while kissing her.
Piyush committed rape on multiple occasions under threat of making her photo viral.
Her daughter NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6829 2 MCRC-55504-2024 complained to her.
Therefore, she is lodging the complaint.
On such allegations, P.S. Malharganj registered FIR for offence punishable under Sections 376, 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 5L, 6 of POCSO Act against Piyush Midtwal.

The statements of witnesses were recorded under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C.
Applicant- Piyush was arrested on 29.6.2024.
He is in custody ever since.
On completion of investigation, final report was submitted.
On DNA examination, y-chromosomal STR DNA profile was not found from the source material of victim.
Trial is underway.

sentences.text: Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the matter.
It is a case of teenage romance between the two adolescents.
The determination of age of the victim during investigation is doubtful.
No offence, as alleged, is committed by the applicant.
False allegations of rape are levelled against the applicant under the pressure of family members of victim.
The DNA report does not implicate the applicant.
Further, the forensic extraction report of the mobile phone seized from possession of the applicant also does not substantiate the prosecution of obscene photo/video.
No criminal antecedents is reported against the applicant.
Applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State ably assisted by the counsel for the objector opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
However, after going through the case diary, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6829 3 MCRC-55504-2024 he fairly states that no criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
Learned counsel for the objector submits that victim in her examination-in-chief has supported the case, but later, in cross- examination supported the defence.

Heard the arguments, perused the grounds for grant of bail stated in the application and the case diary.
The case diary and material on record reveals that initially, the victim has alleged forceful physical relations by applicant, but later, she refused any physical relations with the applicant.
DNA examination report and forensic extraction report of the mobile phone does not support the prosecution.
The veracity of the prosecution and document relating to age of victim will be considered on merits at the trial.
As informed, applicant is aged around 20 years.
He is a street food vendor and is sole bread earner of family.
Considering the age and family status of applicant, there appears to be no possibility of fleeing from justice.

In absence of any criminal antecedent,
considering the socio-economic status of the applicant and the complainant, there appears to be no likelihood of tampering with remaining evidence or influencing the witnesses by the applicant.
The trial would take time to conclude.
There appears to be no compelling reason to continue incarceration of the applicant.
However, it is clarified that the observations, herein above, are recorded for present application only.

Considering the rival contentions and overall circumstances of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:6829 4 MCRC-55504-2024 case, in the light of aforestated facts, but without commenting on the merits, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.

Accordingly, it is directed that applicant - Piyush Midtwal shall be released on bail in connection with the Crime as stated in para-1 of this order, upon furnishing personal bond and surety bond of amount, as may be considered appropriate by the Trial Court for compliance with conditions, as may be imposed by such Court under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C. 1973 / Section 480(3) of BNSS,
2023, to secure presence of the applicant for the trial.
